fixes.explanation: Paran it is, baker! The text says Israel traveled "…from place to place until the cloud settled in the Wilderness of Paran." (Numbers 10:12) That's a whole string of stops before the cloud finally stays put. I've been moved around a lot in my life, and I still wouldn't know when to unpack.

Shur is a decent guess, friend, but the verse points somewhere else. Numbers 10:12 says the cloud settled "…in the Wilderness of Paran." Israel goes from place to place first, and the cloud decides when the trip stops. Nobody in that camp gets to say "are we there yet" and be right.

Ooh, not quite, friend. Picture a group chat where every leader votes on the departure time. That's not what happened here. The text says Israel set out "…according to the LORD’s command through Moses." (Numbers 10:13) The command came from the LORD, and Moses was the one it came through. The tribe leaders just got the memo, and I bet they packed fast.

Water is a smart thing to want after three days of walking, friend. I'd have asked for it too, and for a chair. But that's not Moses' prayer. Whenever the ark sets out, he says, "Rise up, O LORD! May Your enemies be scattered; may those who hate You flee before You." (Numbers 10:35) His words are about the LORD's enemies being scattered, not about supplies.
